standard_prerequisites.name: Connectedness and truncatedness
standard_prerequisites.statement: A type A is n-connected when trunc n A is contractible; a type E is n-truncated when it is an n-type; a path type x =_E y of an (n+1)-truncated type is n-truncated.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement is phrased with n-connectedness, and the proof uses that the path type of an (n+1)-truncated E is n-truncated at source lines 840-842.

standard_prerequisites.name: Suspension as a pushout and truncation of pushouts
standard_prerequisites.statement: The suspension of A is the pushout 1 sqcup^A 1 of the span 1 <- A -> 1, and n-truncation of a pushout cocone is again a pushout among n-truncated types.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof starts by rewriting the goal as contractibility of trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) (source lines 806-809) and then replaces the pushout by the truncated diagram (source lines 811-821).

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of pushouts and the cocone description of a pushout into an n-type
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two pushouts of the same span among n-types are equivalent; and for a span with both legs out of the same object, a cocone with vertex E into an (n+1)-truncated E is the same as a pair of points of E together with a path between them.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof shows that the point 1 is a pushout of the truncated diagram and then applies uniqueness (source lines 823-869).

core_obligations: Rewrite the goal: since the suspension of A is the pushout 1 sqcup^A 1, (n+1)-connectedness of the suspension means contractibility of trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) (source lines 806-809).

Replace that type by a pushout in the (n+1)-truncated types of the diagram obtained by truncating the span, using that truncation commutes with pushouts (source lines 811-814), and then by the pushout of the simplified diagram with vertices 1, using trunc(n+1)1 = 1 (source lines 816-821).

Show that 1 itself is a pushout of that diagram among (n+1)-types: for an (n+1)-truncated E, rewrite the map (1 -> E) -> cocone(D,E) using that (1 -> E) is equivalent to E and that cocone(D,E) is Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x =_E y) (source lines 826-838).

Discharge the remaining factor by observing that trunc(n+1)A is n-connected because trunc n (trunc(n+1)A) = trunc n A = 1, while x =_E y is n-truncated because E is (n+1)-truncated, so the constant-map equivalence applies (source lines 840-845).

Identify Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x =_E y) with E via x -> (x,x,refl_x) to obtain cocone(D,E) = E, hence the equivalence (1 -> E) ~ cocone(D,E), and check that the composite is the map from the beginning (source lines 851-865).
Conclude by uniqueness of pushouts that trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) is 1, which is the (n+1)-connectedness of the suspension (source lines 867-869).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to contractibility of the truncation of the suspension and replace it by a pushout of the truncated, simplified diagram.
Show that the point is a pushout of that diagram: rewrite the cocone type as Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x = y) and use connectedness of the truncated A against truncatedness of the path type.
Identify that total space with E and check the resulting map is the original one.
Apply uniqueness of pushouts to conclude that the truncated suspension is contractible.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 8.2.1 at source lines 801-802: if A is n-connected then its suspension is (n+1)-connected, proved across source lines 805-870. The proof first has to translate the goal into contractibility of trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) (source line 809) and then invoke that truncation of a pushout cocone is a pushout among truncated types to move to the diagram whose vertices are all the point (source lines 811-821). The load-bearing part is the verification that the point is a pushout of that diagram: the cocone type has to be rewritten as Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x =_E y) in two steps, first using that trunc(n+1)A is n-connected while the path type of an (n+1)-truncated E is n-truncated (source lines 840-845), and then using that E is equivalent to that total space (source lines 851-857). Only after that chain can uniqueness of pushouts be applied (source lines 867-869). The statement records none of this: the reduction to a pushout and the two truncation-level bookkeeping steps are the content.
